key_points.text: Elliott Wave Theory is described as the study of price patterns that recur repeatedly in financial markets, of potential use to traders and investors.
R.N. Elliott, an accountant, developed the theory in the early 1930s while bedridden with illness, after spending hours daily studying market charts and noticing recurring patterns in price and time.
R.N. Elliott used the theory to pinpoint the end of the 1929 crash and told people to start buying the market.
In the 1970s, the only way to read R.N. Elliott's original writings was on microfilm, since no full books existed, and the material had nearly been lost to history.
The guest's father had prints made from the microfilm and popularized Elliott Wave Theory during the 1980s.
The theory's peak popularity ('heyday') was in the 1980s.
The father predicted a repeat of the 'roaring 20s' around the late 1970s/early 1980s, contrary to a prevailing doom-and-gloom consensus driven by 18% interest rates and severe inflation.
The guest's first name, Elliott, was chosen in reference to Elliott Wave Theory, with Fibonacci-derived 'Fibbo' as the alternative.
The guest's background is in computer science and engineering, and he had no interest in finance growing up.
The 2008 crash was the moment the guest realized financial analysis has a significant real-world impact on people, not just portfolios.

mechanisms.text: R.N. Elliott identified recurring price-and-time patterns by extensively and repeatedly studying market charts while bedridden with illness, which he later formalized as the Elliott Wave Principle.

arguments.text: High interest rates (18%) and severe runaway inflation made the era's dominant doom-and-gloom consensus understandable, which is what makes the father's contrarian 'roaring 20s repeat' prediction notable.

entities.name: R.N. Elliott (Ralph Nelson Elliott)

entities.name: The guest's father
entities.description: Discovered Elliott Wave Theory via microfilm in the 1970s, had prints made from it, popularized the theory during the 1980s, and predicted a repeat of the 'roaring 20s' against consensus.

entities.name: Elliott (the guest)

concepts.name: Elliott Wave Theory / Elliott Wave Principle
concepts.description: A theory describing recurring price patterns that unfold repeatedly in financial markets, used by traders and investors.

concepts.name: Microfilm access to Elliott's original writings
concepts.description: In the 1970s, R.N. Elliott's writings existed only on microfilm, with no full books available, making the material nearly lost to history until reprinted.

concepts.name: 1929 crash / Great Depression bottom call
concepts.description: The historical market event R.N. Elliott used his theory to analyze, pinpointing its end and recommending buying.

concepts.name: 2008 financial crash
concepts.description: The market event that served as the guest's personal catalyst for taking financial analysis seriously.

open_questions.text: How the guest's father convinced him to continue the family's Elliott Wave work, and how the guest feels about carrying it forward a generation later.

contradictions_or_uncertainty.text: The guest hedges his claim about the worst US inflationary period, qualifying it with 'I think' and noting a possible exception ('maybe the continental').
